LESSON: WRITING 3.3.2 WRITING READINESS (A-E)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.2 Writing readiness (a-e)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.3.2 Writing readiness (a-e), part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we hold our pencils or pens when writing? 2. How do we write letters correctly in the air?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.3.2 Writing readiness (a-e) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: writing skills as learner writes the learnt letter sounds in the air while facing same direction

as the teacher.

● Creativity and imagination: exploration skills as learner models letter sounds for mastery using clay, plasticine or dough.

Values:
● Peace: Responsibility as the learner develops tolerance and takes time to join dots.

● Integrity: Honesty is developed as the learner tries best to write letters on their own even when it seems challenging.

42

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Environmental conservation awareness where the learner learns that even as we learn to write, not every surface is a writing

material (walls, clothes).

Link to other Learning Areas:

Writing is required in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Pencil or colour pencil clay, plasticine or dough, crayons, tracing book
